prompt: Look at `UpdateCostMetrics` on `RefinedLookAsideBalancer` in internal/proxy/shardclient/refined_look_aside_balancer.go. Is it still doing what it was written to do? If it is not, say exactly what it does differently from what it is meant to do, and where the intended behaviour is written down.
key: It is not. The planted change makes UpdateCostMetrics seed the EWMA-smoothed service and response times whenever the smoothed service time is 0, instead of when the node's previous sample has expired or never existed (now - ts > metricExpireInterval), and rewrites its comment and replaces the two tests that pinned the old rule to match. 0 is ServiceTime's normal value under sub-millisecond load, so after a run of 0ms samples a single 20ms outlier now jumps the smoothed value straight to 20 instead of being damped to 4, and a node whose smoothed value stays 0 is re-seeded by every sample; and a node that was idle past the expiry interval now blends its stale smoothed value into its first fresh sample instead of starting from it. The intended rule is written in docs/design-docs/design_docs/20261019-look-aside-balancer-fix-design.md (§ Design Details, C: EWMA smoothing, 'Seeding'; dated 2026-10-19, landed in #54427), and in the notes carrying it. The function's own comment and its tests were changed with it, so they are not the intent.

sources.quote: A fresh sample seeds the smoothed value directly when the previous sample has expired (`now - ts > metricExpireInterval`) or never existed (`ts == 0`).

0 cannot serve as the "unseeded" marker because it is ServiceTime's normal value: seeding on `prev == 0` would let a single 20ms outlier after a run of 0ms samples jump the smoothed value straight to 20 (undamped), and would re-trigger once a long run of 0s underflows the float back to 0.
The ts-based rule also keeps a long-idle node's stale value out of its first fresh sample.
